title: Horde BIN V1 revision 2
description: Minor revision of HORDE_BIN_V1 that gives meaning to two previously reserved bit ranges so tactical-expansion children are distinguishable from self-play line samples. The 48-byte layout, every field offset, every piece code and every V1 invariant are unchanged.

identity_policy.no_expansion: A file generated with expansion disabled carries the HORDE_BIN_V1 name and SHA-256 and is byte-identical to what V1 would have written, header included. Unmodified V1 tooling reads it exactly as before.
identity_policy.expansion: A file generated with expansion enabled carries the HORDE_BIN_V1_R2 name and SHA-256 and three additional generation keys. Unmodified V1 tooling rejects it at the schema identity check, and would reject its child records at the outcome_reason range check even if it did not.
identity_policy.rationale: Fail-closed on the shards that need it, byte-identical on the ones that do not. A reader that does not understand expansion must not train on children as if they were independent self-play samples.

manifest.hash_encoding: Uppercase hexadecimal SHA-256; book_sha256 may be NONE
manifest.canonicalization: Compact JSON with keys emitted in the order documented above. The three expansion keys are appended to the generation object, in the order listed, and are present if and only if the file carries the HORDE_BIN_V1_R2 identity.

fields.name: board
fields.encoding: Two 4-bit piece codes per byte; square 2n is the low nibble and square 2n+1 is the high nibble

expansion.definition: An expansion child is a position reached by making one selected legal move in a written self-play position, then searching it with the same teacher network and the same node or depth budget as its parent.

selection.promotion: Candidates are the legal promotion moves. At most one child per distinct origin-destination pawn push, the first such move in legal-move generation order, capped at expand_promo.
selection.check: Candidates are the legal checking moves that are not promotions, in legal-move generation order, capped at expand_check.
selection.combined_case: A promotion that also gives check belongs to the PROMOTION family and consumes only the promotion budget. The check budget is therefore reserved for non-promoting checks, and no move is counted twice.
selection.ceiling: expand_max_children is a hard per-parent ceiling applied after the per-family caps. The realised maximum is min(expand_promo + expand_check, expand_max_children).
selection.bestmove: The BESTMOVE family value is registered for compatibility with the Spell tactical-expansion lever. The Horde generator does not emit it.

labelling.score: The child score is produced by the same teacher network at the same budget as the parent. Labelling across engine families is forbidden: reported centipawn scales differ.
labelling.result: The child result is the game result seen from the child's own side to move. It is derived from the child position, not by negating the parent record, so no result is fabricated and the records stay lambda-agnostic.
labelling.outcome_reason: The child carries the terminal reason of the game its parent belongs to.

expansion.ordering: Every child immediately follows its parent in the payload, so a reader can recover the (parent, children) unit by scanning forward from a record whose EXPANSION_CHILD bit is clear.

invariants: The board has no white king and exactly one black king.
All physical pawns use PAWN; the legacy H identity is not stored.
White may have up to 36 pieces and the full position may have up to 52 pieces.
Only black castling rights may be present.
best_move and played_move are legal in the stored position.
Every record belongs to a game resolved by Position::outcome; generator truncation is never labeled as a draw.
Per-color insufficient winning material is not an automatic game result.
outcome_reason bits 0-2 are in [1,6] and bits 6-7 are zero.
The EXPANSION_CHILD flag is set if and only if the expansion family is not NONE. A record cannot claim to be a child in one field and a parent in the other.
A file whose manifest carries the HORDE_BIN_V1 identity contains no record with a nonzero expansion family.
